verses.1:1: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah, son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, during the days of Josiah, son of Amon, king of Judah.
verses.1:2: "I will thoroughly sweep away everything from upon the face of the ground," declares the LORD.
verses.1:3: "I will sweep away mankind and animals; I will sweep away the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling blocks along with the wicked; and I will cut off mankind from upon the face of the ground," declares the LORD.
verses.1:4: "And I will stretch out My hand against Judah and against all the residents of Jerusalem, and I will cut off from this place the remnant of Baal, the name of the idolatrous priests together with the priests,
verses.1:5: and those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of the heavens, and those who bow down, who swear to the LORD and swear by their king,
verses.1:6: and those who turn away from following after the LORD, and those who have not sought the LORD and have not inquired of Him."
verses.1:7: Silence before the Lord GOD! For near is the day of the LORD; for the LORD has prepared a sacrifice, He has consecrated His invited guests.
verses.1:8: "And it will happen on the day of the LORD's sacrifice that I will punish the officials and the sons of the king, and all who wear foreign attire.
verses.1:9: And I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold on that day, those who fill the house of their master with violence and deceit."
verses.1:10: "And on that day," declares the LORD, "there will be the sound of an outcry from the Fish Gate, and a wailing from the Second Quarter, and a great crash from the hills.
verses.1:11: Wail, residents of the Mortar, for all the people of Canaan have been silenced; all who are laden with silver have been cut off.
verses.1:12: And it will happen at that time that I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the men who thicken on their dregs, those who say in their hearts, 'The LORD will do no good, nor will He do harm.'
verses.1:13: And their wealth will become plunder, and their houses a desolation; and they will build houses, yet they will not live in them, and they will plant vineyards, yet they will not drink their wine."
verses.1:14: Near is the great day of the LORD, near and hurrying very rapidly! The sound of the day of the LORD! There a mighty warrior cries aloud bitterly.
verses.1:15: That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and anguish, a day of devastation and waste, a day of darkness and blackness, a day of cloud and thick gloom.
verses.1:16: A day of ram's horn and war cry against the fortified cities and against the high corner towers.
verses.1:17: "And I will afflict mankind with distress, and they will walk like blind people, because against the LORD they have sinned; and their blood will be poured out like dust, and their entrails like dung."
verses.1:18: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to rescue them on the day of the LORD's wrath, and by the fire of His jealousy the entire earth will be consumed; for He will make a complete, truly terrifying end of all the residents of the earth.
verses.2:1: Gather yourselves, indeed gather together, shameless nation,
verses.2:2: before the decree gives birth—like chaff the day passes by—before the fierce anger of the LORD comes upon you, before the day of the LORD's anger comes upon you.
verses.2:3: Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, who have practiced His justice; seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on the day of the LORD's anger.
verses.2:4: For Gaza will be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation; at midday they will drive out Ashdod, and Ekron will be uprooted.
verses.2:5: Woe to the residents of the seacoast, nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: "I will destroy you so that there is no resident."
verses.2:6: And the seacoast will become pastures, caves of shepherds, and pens for flocks.
verses.2:7: And the coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; upon them they will graze. In the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down in the evening, for the LORD their God will attend to them and restore their fortunes.
verses.2:8: "I have heard the reproach of Moab and the insults of the sons of Ammon, with which they have reproached My people and acted arrogantly against their border.
verses.2:9: Therefore, as I live," declares the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, "surely Moab will become like Sodom and the sons of Ammon like Gomorrah: a territory of nettles and a pit of salt and a desolation forever. The remnant of My people will despoil them, and the rest of My nation will take possession of them."
verses.2:10: This is what they receive in return for their pride, because they reproached and acted arrogantly against the people of the LORD of hosts.
verses.2:11: The LORD will be fearsome against them, for He will cause all the gods of the earth to waste away, and to Him they will bow down, each one from his own place, all the coastlands of the nations.
verses.2:12: "You also, Cushites, will be struck down by My sword."
verses.2:13: And He will stretch out His hand against the north and destroy Assyria; He will turn Nineveh into a desolation, dry like the wilderness.
verses.2:14: Herds will lie down in her midst, every kind of wild creature; both the desert owl and the screech owl will spend the night on her column capitals. A voice will sing in the window; devastation will be on the threshold, for He has stripped bare the cedarwork.
verses.2:15: This is the exultant city that lived in security, that said in her heart, "I am, and apart from me there is no other." How she has become a waste, a resting place for wild animals! Everyone who passes by her will hiss and wave his hand.
verses.3:1: Woe to the rebellious and defiled one, the oppressing city!
verses.3:2: She has listened to no voice; she has accepted no correction. In the LORD she has not trusted; to her God she has not come near.
verses.3:3: Her officials in her midst are roaring lions; her judges are evening wolves; they save nothing until morning.
verses.3:4: Her prophets are insolent, men of treachery; her priests have profaned what is sacred; they have treated the law with violence.
verses.3:5: The LORD in her midst is righteous; He will commit no injustice. Morning after morning He sets His justice in the light; He never fails. Yet the unjust one knows no shame.
verses.3:6: "I have cut off nations; their corner towers have become desolate. I have laid waste their streets without a passerby; their cities have been devastated, without a man, with no resident.
verses.3:7: I said, 'Surely you will fear Me, you will accept correction,' so that her dwelling would not be cut off in accordance with all that I had appointed against her. Yet indeed they rose early and corrupted all their deeds.
verses.3:8: Therefore wait for Me," declares the LORD, "for the day when I rise up for prey. For My judgment is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out upon them My indignation, all My fierce anger; for by the fire of My jealousy the entire earth will be consumed.
verses.3:9: For then I will turn the peoples to a purified speech, so that all of them may call upon the name of the LORD, to serve Him with one shoulder.
verses.3:10: From across the rivers of Cush, My suppliants, the daughter of My scattered ones, will bring My offering.
verses.3:11: On that day you will not be ashamed over all your deeds by which you transgressed against Me; for then I will remove from your midst those who exult in your pride, and you will no longer be haughty on My holy mountain.
verses.3:12: And I will leave in your midst an afflicted and lowly people, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
verses.3:13: The remnant of Israel will commit no injustice and will speak no falsehood, nor will a tongue of deceit be found in their mouths; for they will graze and lie down, and there will be no one to terrify them."
verses.3:14: Sing for joy, daughter of Zion! Shout triumphantly, Israel! Be glad and exult with a whole heart, daughter of Jerusalem!
verses.3:15: The LORD has removed the judgments against you; He has turned away your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you will fear calamity no longer.
verses.3:16: On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: "Do not fear; Zion, do not let your hands drop slack.
verses.3:17: The LORD your God is in your midst, a mighty warrior who saves; He will delight over you with gladness, He will be still in His love, He will rejoice over you with joyful singing."
verses.3:18: "I will gather those grieving away from the appointed festival; from you they came; reproach was a burden upon her.
verses.3:19: Look, at that time I am going to deal with all your oppressors; and I will save the lame and gather the outcast, and I will turn them into praise and renown in every land of their shame.
verses.3:20: At that time I will bring you in—yes, at the time when I gather you—for I will appoint you for renown and praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes," says the LORD.

notes.1:2: Hebrew pairs the Qal infinitive absolute of asap ("gather/remove") with the Hiphil imperfect of sup ("bring to an end/sweep away"), creating an emphatic wordplay meaning "thoroughly sweep away."
notes.1:3: Hebrew hammakselot ("the stumbling blocks," from kasal, "stumble") can refer either to idolatrous objects that cause sin or to heaps of ruins.
notes.1:5: Masoretic bemalkam reads "by their king," probably alluding to the Ammonite god Milcom, whose name the Syriac and Vulgate read here.
notes.1:11: "The Mortar" translates hammaktes (Maktesh), a basin-shaped commercial district of Jerusalem; "people of Canaan" idiomatically denotes traders, paired with netile kasep (Qal passive participle of natal, "laden with silver" or "weighing out silver").
notes.1:12: "Thicken on their dregs" translates the Qal participle of qapa ("congeal/thicken") with semarim ("dregs/lees"), a winemaking image depicting undisturbed complacency.
notes.2:1: The imperative pair hitqosesu waqossu (Hithpolel and Qal imperatives of qasas, literally "gather stubble") intensifies the call to assemble; lo niksap (Niphal of kasap) is commonly understood via Aramaic and late Hebrew as "shameless," though in Biblical Hebrew kasap also means "long for" (hence "undesired").
notes.2:4: The verse employs two Hebrew sound-plays: azza azuba ("Gaza ... forsaken") and eqron teager ("Ekron will be uprooted," Niphal of aqar).
notes.2:6: Hebrew kerot is uncertain, derived either from kara ("dig," hence "caves/cisterns") or from kar ("meadow"), while echoing "Cherethites" (keretim) in verse 5.
notes.2:7: Ketiv reads sebutam and qere reads sebitam, two orthographic variants of the same noun in the idiom sub sebit/sebut, meaning "restore their fortunes" (literally "turn back their captivity/turning").
notes.2:14: Hebrew hayto-goy (literally "beast of a nation") denotes wild creatures of every kind; the exact species of qaat and qippod are uncertain, and the translation follows the Masoretic readings qol ("a voice") and horeb ("devastation") rather than the Septuagint.
notes.3:3: Hebrew lo garemu (Qal perfect of garam, related to gerem, "bone") literally means "they do not leave a bone" or "they save nothing" until morning.
notes.3:8: The Masoretic text reads lead ("for prey/plunder"), whereas the Septuagint reflects a different vocalization, leed ("as a witness").
notes.3:9: Hebrew ehpok el-ammim sapa berura literally reads "I will turn/change to peoples a purified lip," and sekem ehad ("one shoulder") is an idiom for united service.
notes.3:17: Following the Masoretic text, yaharis (Hiphil imperfect of haras) means "He will be still/silent" in deep love, whereas the Septuagint reflects yehaddes ("He will renew").
notes.3:18: The Masoretic text is terse and shifts grammatical person from second feminine singular (mimmek, "from you") to third feminine singular (aleha, "upon her"); nuge is the Niphal participle construct of yaga ("those grieving"), and asapti ("I will gather") functions as a prophetic perfect.
